To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Wikipedia's reliability is high and that its reliability varies across articles, and that the reliability of the text in Wikipedia can be quantified and used to inform readers.
we have developed an approach that can be used to compute trust for Wikipedia content, and that this approach is effective at predicting human judgments of trust.

we have developed a method for computing trust for text that is based on the Wikipedia's own history of editing and that we have demonstrated the effectiveness of this method by using it to identify reliable and unreliable text within the Wikipedia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of assigning trust values to text in Wikipedia articles.

1) the design of a system for automatically assigning trust values to Wikipedia content; 2) the development of a model that can be used to predict the reliability of text in the Wikipedia, and 3) the design and evaluation of a user interface for presenting the trust values.

developing methods that allow Wikipedia users to evaluate the trustworthiness of the information they are reading. We are developing a tool to support the Wikipedia users in their decision making process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wikipedia articles have a high degree of trustworthiness.
the Wikipedia is a valuable source of information, with a high level of trustworthiness, and a low level of bias.
our method is a useful and reliable tool to assess trust in Wikipedia articles, and it is a step forward in the development of tools for trust assessment in collaborative knowledge bases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Wikipedia is an open encyclopedia that can be used as a reference source, but its content should not be used uncritically.
we propose a system that allows the user to assign a trust value to a piece of Wikipedia text, and that the trust values are computed using the Wikipedia's own history of editing.
the Wikipedia is a collaborative and reliable source of information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trust values computed from the Wikipedia's own text are a useful tool for readers.
the trust values can be used as a guide for readers to make informed decisions about the reliability of text.
the Wikipedia is not a homogeneous source: there is text in Wikipedia articles that is more reliable than other text.
